pr_title: drivers: timer: arm_arch_timer fix tick-less bug
pr_body:
Calculation of compare value was getting clipped due to '32b' and 'signed'
typecasts. This resulted in very short next cycle compare value instead
of maximum possible ticks.
  
fixes: #26476
Signed-off-by: Sandeep Tripathy <sandeep.tripathy@broadcom.com>
pr_comments: Tested on Qemu. This version takes care of all cases and works fine.

>  whether the tick configuration is such that an overflow is possible

a-
Since in this case `MAX_TICKS` is not capped at `INT_MAX/UINT_MAX`  It is possible to go beyond `32b`  in ~5days (unlikely as other timer usage will be there to have the timeout) in case of `K_FOREVER`.
And subsequently have `last_count `wrong. This can be fixed by not truncating the delta_ticks calculation. Thanks! this truncation 
was unnecessary. But do we assume max ticks to be 32b  see  `uint32_t z_clock_elapsed() `  Or
b-
Now I am wondering should I cap platform `MAX_TICKS` to `INT_MAX`. ie `K_FOREVER` is about  `~59` hours  (default ticks per sec is `10000` for `tick-less`) . Because  `z_clock_elapsed() ` assumes max value to be `INT_MAX` ?  This will have everything under control. But even with K_FOREVER  timer interrupt will fire in couple of days which is quite acceptable I think.

  I am actually not sure why the MAX_WAIT calculation in `kernel/timeout.c` is differentiating `K_FOREVER`.
```
#define MAX_WAIT (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SYSTEM_CLOCK_SLOPPY_IDLE) \
                  ? K_TICKS_FOREVER : INT_MAX)
```
I should do one of  'a' or 'b'

Good points; this probably isn't right yet.

> I am actually not sure why the MAX_WAIT calculation in `kernel/timeout.c` is differentiating `K_FOREVER`.

I can answer this part, though perhaps not correctly.  `SYSTEM_CLOCK_SLOPPY_IDLE` is an under-defined feature that allows the system clock to become non-linear in tickless mode when there's no next timeout available.  One use case for this is to turn off the timer to save power.

AFAICT it's receipt of `K_TICKS_FOREVER` as the `ticks` parameter that triggers this feature: in at least some configurations its value can be distinguished from `INT_MAX`.  A couple drivers including `arcv2_timer0` and `cortex_m_systick` seem to do this, though neither condition it on `SYSTEM_CLOCK_SLOPPY_IDLE`.

> I should do one of 'a' or 'b'

On further thought I'm pretty sure Zephyr needs to be notified with tick counts that won't wrap, and since `z_clock_announce()` takes an `int32_t` the value of `MAX_TICKS` should be capped at `INT32_MAX` for all platforms.  Or maybe a little less, in case the announcement gets delayed and the internal calculation wraps, though I don't think anybody does that.  So, 'b'.

> On further thought I'm pretty sure Zephyr needs to be notified with tick counts that won't wrap

That can potentially achieve ~59h of silence on ticks. Acceptable for all practical purpose. I am going ahead with the capping of MAX_TICKS to INT_MAX. Thanks a lot for the inputs.

issue_context.title: ARM Cortex-A: architecture timer continuously firing in tick-less mode
issue_context.body:
arm architecture timer interrupt is PPI to GIC cpu interface and level sensitive.
the interrupt request is cleared from IP upon 1- disabling the timer Or 2- updating the compare value Or 3-masking the interrupt.

In current driver we update the compare value to Next tick value in Tick mode.  This is working fine.
In Tick-less mode the next value should be updated as well. And that happens in` z_clock_announce().`
Still there is continuous firing of timer interrupt in tick-less mode. So in this path the timer interrupt clear is
no happening Or the compare value is not updated.  I need to check that.

If we configure the interrupt to edge sensitive the issue will not be seen on Qemu.
comments:
If I mask the timer interrupt in ISR as part of interrupt clearing it works fine. That will require a refactor of the timer driver.
But I am not sure why compare value update does not work as such.

Depending on compare value to clear the interrupt means we arm an interrupt far in future.
ie. K_FOREVER/MAX_WAIT etc.. should be max possible ticks on the architecture. 
Due to typecasts and some calculations thats not happening in current code. 
Will tyr a quick fix and update a PR. That will not change the current approach of
updating compare value to clear interrupt.

However in future it will be better to use the IMASK to clear the interrupt.

review_comments:
FWIW: sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec() is a C API that is identical to CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_HW_CYCLES_PER_SEC on all platforms except the hpet driver on x86.  There's not a lot of value to using it here, it probably got cut-and-pasted from another timer driver, which was itself probably modified via a script when the wrapper API was introduced.

Really hardware frequency values like this want to be coming from devicetree anyway.

Noted. 
Typically we would read the counter frequency from Cortex-A core register cntfrq which is expected to be programmed by EL3 stage. ie. It could be pre-boot firmware or arch code in zephyr it self.  Maybe another PR someday.
